39.title: Scientific acceptance: finite CPU and Vulkan Schwarzschild/Kerr profile
39.body:
**Passed finite scientific acceptance** at **`5e706073a3fd2f9afcf8efbcde2f094122050f6a`**, 2026-10-03. This is a finite numerical profile of the implemented Schwarzschild/Kerr instrument, including actual Vulkan execution. It preserves the broader specification. The deterministic inputs and independent references are checked into this revision; the results below delimit the claim.

### Capability and metric disposition

| Registered metric | Implementation disposition | This scientific profile |
|---|---|---|
| Minkowski | CPU and Vulkan | Analytic moving-observer, pupil, straight-ray and beam controls |
| Schwarzschild | CPU and retained Vulkan | Finite camera-to-capture/escape/disk rays, beams, frequency, relative thin/grey-volume emission |
| Kerr | CPU and retained Vulkan | The same finite transport contracts; moving observers, turning rays and near-extremal controls; bounded point-source detector flux |
| Reissner–Nordstrom | CPU; Einstein–Maxwell local metric checks | Implemented, outside this profile; full transport/observable accuracy unqualified |
| Kerr–Newman | CPU; Einstein–Maxwell local metric checks | Implemented, outside this profile; full transport/observable accuracy unqualified |
| de Sitter | CPU; positive-lambda finite causal patch | Implemented, outside this profile; cosmological transport accuracy unqualified |
| Schwarzschild–de Sitter | CPU; positive-lambda sub-Nariai sector | Implemented, outside this profile; full transport accuracy unqualified |
| Morris–Thorne | CPU/Vulkan exact zero-tidal Ellis geometry; declared one/two-sheet topology | Implemented, outside this profile; full transport accuracy unqualified |
| Alcubierre | CPU/Vulkan declared moving tanh-wall geometry and bounded parameters | Implemented, outside this profile; full transport accuracy unqualified |

CPU thin-disk linear polarisation is included under its declared pure-scattering atmosphere. Vulkan and volumetric polarisation explicitly decline and receive no numerical polarisation claim. Local geometry checks or a completed frame do not qualify the other metrics scientifically. DNGR fidelity, uniform critical/caustic accuracy, high-resolution images, hardware budgets, GPU throughput and full release qualification remain outside this milestone.

### Conventions and reference independence

Geometric quantities use `G=c=1`, signature `(-+++)`, coordinate-length mass `M` and dimensional spin `a`. Public scenes retain `0.1 <= M <= 100`, `0 <= a/M <= 0.998` and their existing observer/camera admission rules; the observations cover the finite witnesses below, rather than every input in those intervals. The camera is the metric-aware ADM/Eulerian observer, with explicitly supplied local boosts and virtual pupil offsets. Past-directed launch tangents have unit camera frequency. Escape/disk endpoints return to the native ingoing Kerr–Schild chart; past horizon endpoints retain the regular outgoing chart. A physical terminal event is distinct from cancellation, budget exhaustion and numerical failure.

The independent full-path reference evolves the separated Carter equations in Mino time with RK4, including radial/polar turning, independent chart transforms and event roots, and a separately refined infinity quadrature. It does not use the production Hamiltonian/connection/integrator or its terminal event to generate the expected trajectory. The production launch event/tangent is a measured initial condition; analytic observer-frame and film-differential controls separately qualify that join. Four-point independent ray differences along each of the two camera angular axes supply the screen covariance and canonical finite/infinity angular derivatives. Formulation: [Gralla & Lupsasca, equations 3–9](https://arxiv.org/html/1910.12881v3). Reference arithmetic is extended `long double` on GCC and binary64 on MSVC; each platform must pass its explicit reference-refinement bounds.

Frequency means `g = nu_observer/nu_emitter`. Relative TrueColor disk RGB uses the declared normalised Planck hue and a single `(g*T_profile)^4` bolometric factor; it is not calibrated SI RGB. The independent grey-volume reference separately integrates opacity, comoving path length and attenuated relative source in a reduced radial ODE. Its independent Page–Thorne angular-momentum derivative/integral uses finite differences and Simpson quadrature, including the declared dark inner buffer; see [Page & Thorne (1974)](https://articles.adsabs.harvard.edu/pdf/1974ApJ...191..499P). Planck expectations use SI defining constants, an independently evaluated declared CIE fit and inverse RGB transform. Point-source flux uses the fixed observed 380–780 nm band, catalogue normalisation, canonical angular-map area and the normalised compact Gaussian detector. CPU polarisation uses an algebraic Walker–Penrose reconstruction between measured launch screens and the actual disk event, with independently evaluated Boyer–Lindquist contractions; trajectory correctness is supplied separately by the Carter corpus. See [James et al. (2015)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1502.03808). Shared CPU/device equations are never the physics oracle.

### Frozen corpus, controls and conditioning

The [full-path cases](https://github.com/sunyaisblank/Sirius/blob/666aa9593eee38b74e65d290fef85c16a9837b04/tests/backend/full_path_acceptance_test.cpp) contain 11 launches at three refinements: moving/pupil Minkowski; Schwarzschild capture `b/M=2`, turning `b/M=8, M=0.1`, and near-critical escape `b/M=3*sqrt(3)+0.05`; Kerr `a/M=0.7` moving off-plane escape and `0.998` inward turning; direct differential controls `a/M=-0.998, M=100`, exact `a/M=+1` capture and `-1` outward; and Schwarzschild/Kerr `0.998` transverse first disk crossings in `6..20 M`. The signed/exact-extremal direct controls do not extend the public scene domain. All directions, boosts, radii and pupils are frozen in that test.

Production `(maximum affine step/M, abs=rel tolerance)` is `(2,5e-6)`, `(0.5,5e-8)`, `(0.125,5e-10)`, with minimum step `1e-6 M` and 20,000 attempts. Independent reference step fractions are `0.002/0.001`, tightened to `0.001/0.0005` for the critical witness; infinity panels double `2048/4096` or `4096/8192`. Angular stencils halve independently. The reference must stabilise below `1e-6`, one percent of the pre-existing `1e-4` position/angular accuracy budget. Endpoint error is the maximum of coordinate/affine error divided by `M` and tangent-component error; angles are radians; each matrix error is the maximum entry difference divided by the expected matrix maximum norm. Nonfinite values fail. Beam axes/area are physical screen lengths/area; the canonical angular map is a distinct observable.

Analytic beam regressions cover anisotropy, output-plane orientation, exact rank loss, adjacent representable full rank, compensated determinant residuals and wide binary exponents. The independently differenced covariance does not certify relative minor-axis error arbitrarily close to a caustic. The moving Kerr point-source witness bounds map condition number below 2.62, places its image inside the detector support, and freezes the catalogue float direction before independent image inversion. Its 1,024-probe and 4,096-cell budget completes with 81 cells and 603/603/604 probes at three root/flux refinements. It makes no uniform critical-image flux claim.

The volume witness uses observer `30 M`, annulus `6..20 M`, `H/r=0.1`, optical-depth scale `0.2`, temperature scale 30,000 K, and Schwarzschild radial/Kerr principal rays at spins `0.7/0.998`. Both declared temperature models are compared with independent 4,096/8,192-panel transport. Production `(maximum affine step, midpoint samples)` is `(0.5,8)`, `(0.25,32)`, `(0.125,128)`, with geodesic abs/rel `1e-9` and 10,000 attempts. The finest profile must achieve relative optical-depth/channel error below `5e-4`. Hard support edges make sample spacing a separate accuracy control; geodesic tolerances alone and default volume settings do not receive this bound. Optically thin and exact optical-depth-cap controls preserve physical ray fate.

The end-to-end thin-disk check publishes ungraded linear channels from the actual typed CPU session and Vulkan `RenderVulkanToDisplay` path. It uses 3x3, one sample, Schwarzschild and moving Kerr `0.7`, the selected Shakura–Sunyaev profile at 12,000 K, independent first Carter crossings, ISCO/emitter contractions and thermal channels, judging four interior transverse pixels at `1e-4`. CPU polarisation traces nine disk crossings at spins `0/0.7/0.998`, steps `0.4/0.2/0.1`, tolerances `1e-7/1.25e-8/1.5625e-9`; normal and nearby emission additionally check finite Stokes continuity.

### Quantitative acceptance

Maxima across all cases and all three refinements (reference uncertainty is checked separately and added to the acceptance comparison):

| Full-path error measure | CPU | Radeon binary32 products | Radeon binary64 products | Bound |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Endpoint/affine per M and tangent components | 1.862e-8 | 1.667e-8 | 1.667e-8 | 1e-4 |
| Direction angle, rad | 6.202e-10 | 5.547e-10 | 5.547e-10 | 1e-4 |
| Finite angular map, fractional matrix norm | 7.949e-9 | 2.523e-9 | 2.523e-9 | 1e-4 |
| Infinity angular map, fractional matrix norm | 6.028e-9 | 6.039e-10 | 6.039e-10 | 1e-4 |
| Physical beam covariance, fractional matrix norm | 1.191e-7 | 1.190e-7 | 1.190e-7 | 1e-4 |
| Independent endpoint refinement gap | 2.780e-7 | 2.805e-7 | 2.805e-7 | 1e-6 |
| Independent map refinement gap | 1.274e-7 | 1.334e-7 | 1.334e-7 | 1e-6 |

| Observable | CPU maximum error | Radeon maximum error | Criterion |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Finest grey-volume optical depth, relative | 7.837e-6 | 7.837e-6 | 5e-4 |
| Finest grey-volume RGB channel, relative | 1.415e-6 | 1.415e-6 | 5e-4 |
| Moving Kerr detector flux, relative channel | 3.350e-7 | 3.331e-7 | finest 1e-4 |
| Published thin-disk channel / reference peak | 4.247e-7 | 4.247e-7 | 1e-4 |
| CPU disk EVPA, rad | 1.459e-8 | Explicitly unsupported | 1e-4 |

Volume aggregate errors at its three levels are `1.524e-3 -> 8.590e-4 -> 7.837e-6` (Schwarzschild), `2.027e-3 -> 2.600e-4 -> 4.617e-6` (Kerr0.7), and `2.569e-3 -> 3.144e-4 -> 6.978e-6` (Kerr0.998). The independent volume reference gap is at most `7.177e-8`; detector reference gaps are `2.365e-11` (CPU) and `3.846e-9` (MSVC/Radeon). The isolated dark-buffer optical-depth error is `1.437e-8`; temperature half/double controls give the required `1/16` and `16` source ratios. Published disk reference RGB/endpoint/frequency gaps across CPU and Radeon are at most `5.015e-10`, `2.663e-9 M`, and `4.496e-11`.

Full-path endpoint and infinity-map refinements obey the explicit non-worsening allowance for reference/roundoff plateaus; every measured output meets its bound at every refinement. These observations do not establish a convergence order for all outputs. Volume errors improve under the declared independent segment/sample controls. CPU EVPA and detector flux are already at their represented field/reference plateaus; tightening controls does not support an invented convergence slope.

Existing independent metric/inverse, Schwarzschild limits, analytic observer/film controls, frequency/intensity transformations and critical/budget/event failure checks passed in the aggregate. CPU live accepted-ray controls measure worst relative energy/angular-momentum drift below `1e-4`, Carter drift below `1e-4` for the off-plane near-extremal witness, and absolute null residual below `1e-6`. Retained Vulkan independently uses a normalized pre-projection null admission threshold of `1e-6`, then compares complete terminal position/tangent, events and maps against the Carter corpus. This profile does not claim a separately measured maximum interior retained energy/angular-momentum/Carter drift. Source traces verify the shared host event and observable joins; the actual retained Vulkan tests require positive camera/interval execution counts and comparison against the independent references.

### Revision, builds and reproduction

The final source revision above is integrated into clean, pushed `main`. CPU aggregate and detailed numerical observations bind to `5e70607`. Radeon backend and detector observations reuse clean `666aa95` evidence; its physics, reference and backend/detector test sources are unchanged at `5e70607`. The original disk fixture was rejected before physics comparison for CPU-only tile/thread controls; its diagnostic report is retained. The only intervening source change restores admitted Vulkan defaults in that fixture; that corrected check and final build/governance/CPU aggregate bind to `5e70607`. No numerical criterion changed. Local `linux-gcc` Release used GCC 14.2.0, Slang 2026.12.0.1/SPIR-V tools, enforced contracts and warnings as errors. **136 focused CPU numerical/boundary tests passed, zero failed/skipped, 110.79 s.** The exact revision also passed complete strict Linux, Windows and macOS product/test builds and their non-render authority controls in [workflow 37094910047](https://github.com/sunyaisblank/Sirius/actions/runs/37094910047). Source/alignment governance and formatting gates also passed. Native build evidence is not a full runtime/release attestation. The automatic [push-triggered full qualification run](https://github.com/sunyaisblank/Sirius/actions/runs/37095861934) was cancelled to keep this milestone within its agreed scope; the exact-revision strict integration workflow above passed.

Actual Vulkan device: **AMD Radeon 780M**, native Windows driver **AMD proprietary 26.8.1 (LLPC)**, API **1.4.349**, driver version **2.0.395**, vendor/device **1002/1900**. Binary32 subnormal preservation and binary32/binary64 round-to-nearest controls are reported and required. Retained full-path acceptance executes both binary32-product and binary64-product modes of the three-term binary32 retained transport (two-term camera); live volume, detector and published disk comparisons use the default retained binary32 mode. The Windows executables/resources are byte-identical to verified revision-bound native bundles from [666aa95 workflow](https://github.com/sunyaisblank/Sirius/actions/runs/37092841645) for unchanged ray/volume/detector checks and the final workflow for the corrected disk/projection checks; no arithmetic/admission/resource guard was bypassed. Full-path device work is 66 complete traces with a maximum 1,052 attempts per ray (CPU: 33 traces, maximum 2,409); recorded wall time 343.870 s, volume 67.317 s (2,674 interval batches), detector 196.295 s (1,810 camera/7,238 interval batches). Detector stage counts are 42,210/33,768/25,368, with tail attempts 3,515/3,515/3,521. These timings describe this acceptance workload, not a throughput benchmark. The corrected published-disk check passed in 86.695 s; independent frozen endpoint projection/continuation/idempotence/invalid-row controls passed in 36.280 s (1e-11 local comparison criterion).

Reproduce from this revision using the existing presets, writing disposable output under `out/`:

```sh

cmake --build --preset linux-gcc --target sirius_core_tests sirius_oracle_tests sirius_backend_tests sirius_render_tests SiriusAlignmentGate SiriusSourceGovernance

```

The final 136-case CPU aggregate uses:

```sh
ctest --test-dir bin/linux-gcc --output-on-failure --no-tests=error --output-junit out/acceptance-cpu.xml -R '^(SchwarzschildTests|KerrTests|TensorInverseTests|ObserverFrameTests|CameraFilmDifferential|CameraContinuousProjection|LivePathConservationTests|CaptureSurfaceTests|RetainedArithmetic|SpectralValidationTests|PointSourceTransfer|CpuJacobiOracle|PolarisationAcceptance|VolumeAcceptance|KerrInfinity|KerrZamoTransfer|PointSourceDetector)\.|^FullPathAcceptance\.Cpu|^RenderSessionProbe\.(CpuThinDiskPublished|TypedNumericBoundaries|PolarisedRequestsDecline)|^VulkanRenderSession\.CapabilityBoundaryRejectsUnrepresentedSceneSemantics|^AnalyticValidationTest\.PageThorne|^BeamPropagationTest\.(BeamGeometryExtraction|Caustic)|^CpuTraceBoundary\.(Cancellation|UnrepresentedPast|PastRadial|LateMinimum|RejectedOutward|OrdinaryEscape|JacobiBundle)|^CoupledTransport\.(OriginalCritical|NonfiniteColumns|SkyMapIsIndependent)' -E 'RetainedVulkan|RetainedMovingKerr|LargeSharedRegion'
```

On native Windows with the admitted driver, configure/build `windows-msvc` Release (or verify/download the existing workflow's exact native bundle and restore its bound runtime resources), then run:

```powershell
bin/windows-msvc/tests/backend/Release/sirius_backend_tests.exe --gtest_filter=FullPathAcceptance.VulkanRetainedIndependentCarterEventsMapsAndRefinement:VolumeAcceptance.RetainedVulkanRadialObservablesMatchIndependentTransfer:RetainedComputeTest.ProjectedEndpointsKeepPhysicalColumnsAndRetainedContinuation --gtest_output=xml:out/backend-vulkan.xml

```

The checked-in [separated trajectory](https://github.com/sunyaisblank/Sirius/blob/666aa9593eee38b74e65d290fef85c16a9837b04/tests/support/separated_geodesic_reference.h) and [spectral band](https://github.com/sunyaisblank/Sirius/blob/666aa9593eee38b74e65d290fef85c16a9837b04/tests/support/point_source_band_reference.h) helpers, volume/polarisation tests and existing layered controls contain all minimal inputs/reference algorithms and frozen tolerances. Google Test XML properties record per-case errors, reference gaps, controls and work counts. The retained numerical XML, CPU aggregate report and verified Windows bundle are retained locally under `attestations/scientific-core/{666aa95,5e70607}/`; this issue is the single prose acceptance record.

Repairs: #40 stable scaled beam axes/orientation/determinant, #41 relative thermal amplitude and dark-layer extinction, #42 finite unpolarised normal-emission Stokes. Commits `7f5f217` and `666aa95` preserve those regressions; `5e70607` supplies admitted Vulkan fixture controls. This acceptance does not claim absence of all possible defects.

Environment limitation retained in the evidence: Linux llvmpipe lacks required binary32 subnormal preservation and correctly refuses retained acceptance. Its direct shader geometry controls pass but do not qualify the retained renderer. An initial cold software-Vulkan infinity submission exceeded the unchanged 1,000 ms dispatch governor; the focused warm recheck passed. No performance threshold, numerical tolerance or supported-mode guard was relaxed.
